questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

Evolutionary processes give rise to biodiversity in every (1)/ level of biological organisation, including the level of (2)/ species, individual organisms, and molecules. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **1- the error lies only in Part 1.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

It should be **on every level **instead of *in*.

A level is analogous to a floor of a building. And we say *my office is **on **the third floor*.

Option 1 is thus the correct answer.

**The correct sentence**: Evolutionary processes give rise to biodiversity ***on*** every level of biological organisation, including the level of species, individual organisms, and molecules.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in ****correct**** order.**

The elusive

P: status in the Red List of the International

Q: snow leopard has lost its endangered

R: Union for Conservation of Nature
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **QPR.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

Elusive means difficult to find or catch. Now, what could be difficult to find?

 
• Clearly, out of P, Q, and R, Q starts with *snow leopard *which fits the description, **so Q is the first part.**

 
 
• Automatically options 2 and 4 are ruled out.
 
 
 
• A sentence can't end with **of the international, so** P can't be the last part.
 
• Hence Option 1) *QPR *is the correct answer.

**The sentence: The elusive snow leopard has lost its endangered status in the Red List of the International Union for Conservation of Nature.**

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice. **

He gave her promotion happily.

options.text: She was given promotion happily by him.
She had been given promotion by him happily.
Her promotion was gave happily by him.

questions.solution: The given sentence is in **simple past tense**. Thus, the passive voice will be **was/were + past participle of give = *given****. *Option 1) *She was given promotion happily by him *is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech. **

Anuj said, “I need your help now.”

options.text: Anuj said that he needed my help then.
Anuj said he needed my help now.
Anuj says he needed my help now.

questions.solution: Then => now during change of speech => rule out 3) and 4). You can't eliminate the information that these were the words said by Anuj => rule out 1). Option 2) *Anuj said that he needed my help then *is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement". **

Over the last few weeks I (has been) on a whirlwind series of travel for work and vacation.
questions.solution:
*I *takes **have**, not has. Rule out 4). 2) and 3) are grammatically incorrect phrases. Option 1) *Have been *is the correct answer.

Correct phrases in place of 2,3 = **was being** and **have been**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement". **

I closed the window just in time and (return) to my room with relief.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Returned.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

The first part of the sentence(the first clause) is in the simple past tense and to maintain uniformity and parallelism, the verb in the second clause must also be in the same tense as the actions are considered almost simultaneous. 

**The correct sentence**: I closed the window just in time and returned to my room with relief.
